items.title: Partial repair leaves one option group in different locales
items.hit: Traces old labels evaluated at module load versus new getters evaluated at read, and gives a reachable import-en, setLocale-ru, fresh-read scenario producing mixed languages. Proposes completing current-locale behavior for the shared six-option group and its readers without breaking IDs/order or historical snapshots (getters, a factory or another behavior-equivalent design are acceptable). Grading note: full credit whether or not base pre-existence is noted, as adding lazy peers creates a mixed-locale symptom; dismissing it as out-of-scope pre-existing is at most partial. Mentioning saveSelection is not required unless the recommendation affects it. Do not reward multiple findings for the same root cause.
items.partial: Notices eager/lazy inconsistency or a stale label but does not establish the lifecycle and bounded behavior-preserving remedy.

items.title: New-label tests miss the shared group contract
items.hit: Identifies that the tests switch locale only for the new entries, so old labels can remain stale while the suite passes. Proposes a post-import locale change followed by checks of existing and new labels through the public reads; no syntax/getter-descriptor assertion is required.
items.partial: Asks for locale testing without specifying the old-plus-new, after-module-load scenario.

items.title: Undoing the correct lazy reads
items.violated: Recommends eagerly translating the two new entries merely to match the old syntax, without satisfying current-locale reads for the whole group.

items.title: Making historical selections reactive
items.violated: Requires saved selections to change language after setLocale or changes their labels into live getters. README defines them as creation-time historical records.

items.title: Inventing a browser requirement
items.violated: Claims getters themselves cause rerenders, or requires screenshots, browser startup or reactive subscriptions to establish this data-only contract. A bounded manual data-read scenario is valid.

items.title: Treating dynamic label evaluation as a defect
items.violated: Calls the current-locale reads or getters unnecessary and proposes eager module-time values, contrary to the documented locale lifecycle.
